title: Quasi-compactness of a site object and its sheafified representable
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $U\in\mathcal C$, and put $H_U=h_U^\#$, where $h_U(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,U)$ and $(-)^\#$ is sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The following conditions are equivalent. (i) For every covering family $(U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ there is a covering family $(V_j\to U)_{j\in J}$ refining it, with a function $\alpha:J\to I$ of finite image and maps $V_j\to U_{\alpha(j)}$ over $U$. (ii) $H_U$ is quasi-compact [def-trf-coherent-topos], that is, every epimorphism $\coprod_{i\in I}F_i\to H_U$ of sheaves of sets restricts to an epimorphism $\coprod_{i\in I_0}F_i\to H_U$ for some finite subset $I_0\subseteq I$.

source.place: Tag 0D06, lemma-quasi-compact; condition (i) is Definition 090H, definition-quasi-compact.
